4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Present simple: affirmative and negative

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use the present simple for habits and facts (costumbres y verdades)
  • Add -s or -es with he, she and it
  • Make negative sentences with don't and doesn't
  • Write true sentences about you and your family
  • Say what you like, love and hate with -ing
  • Pronounce the -s ending: /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/
  • Use the present simple for facts about the world
  • Write a description of a family member

Para pensar

En inglés decimos «I play», «you play», «we play»… pero «she plays». ¿De dónde sale esa s?

Explicación

1. When do we use it?

We use the present simple for things that happen again and again (habits): «I walk to school every day», «We play football on Saturdays». We also use it for things that are always true (facts): «Cows eat grass», «The sun rises in the east».

En castellano: es como nuestro presente cuando hablamos de costumbres: «como fruta todos los días», «los gatos duermen mucho». No sirve para lo que está pasando justo ahora; para eso hay otro tiempo que verás más adelante.

2. I, you, we, they: easy!

With I, you, we and they, the verb doesn't change. It's the same word you find in the dictionary: «I like apples», «You like apples», «We like apples», «They like apples».

This is great news! In Spanish we say «me gusta, te gusta, nos gusta…», with different endings. In English, for four persons, the verb is exactly the same. Remember that you means «tú» and also «vosotros»: «You live in Bilbao» can be one person or a group.

3. He, she, it: add -s

With he, she and it we add -s to the verb: «He plays the guitar», «She reads comics», «It rains a lot in Galicia».

This also happens with names and with one person or thing: «Marta swims», «My dad cooks», «The dog barks». A good trick: if you can change the subject for he, she or it, put the -s. En castellano: piensa en la «s» como una pegatina que solo llevan él, ella y ello.

4. Like, love, hate + -ing

To talk about what we like and don't like, we use these verbs with a noun or a verb in -ing:

  • love (encantar) ❤️❤️: «I love swimming.»
  • like (gustar) ❤️: «I like reading.»
  • don't mind (no me importa) 😐: «I don't mind doing homework.»
  • don't like (no gustar) 👎: «I don't like cleaning my room.»
  • hate (odiar) 👎👎: «I hate getting up early.»

Notice: after these verbs, the next verb takes -ing: like swimming, love dancing, hate waiting.

With he, she and it, remember the -s:

  • «She loves drawing.»
  • «He likes playing chess.»
  • «My cat hates having a bath!»
  • «She doesn't like football.» (Negative: doesn't + verb without -s.)

Questions:

  • «Do you like singing?» → «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»
  • «Does your brother like pizza?» → «Yes, he does.»

Be careful: in Spanish we say me gusta, but in English the person goes first: «I like…», not «Me like…».

5. Spelling: -s, -es, -ies

Most verbs just add -s: play → plays, like → likes, eat → eats. But verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x and -o add -es: watch → watches, wash → washes, go → goes, do → does.

Verbs ending in consonant + y change to -ies: study → studies, fly → flies. But if there is a vowel before the y, just add -s: play → plays. And one special verb: have → has. «She has a brother.»

6. Negative: don't

To say no, we put don't (do not) before the verb: «I don't like spiders», «We don't go to school on Sunday», «They don't eat meat».

We use don't with I, you, we, they. En castellano: es nuestro «no»: «no me gustan las arañas». Pero fíjate: en inglés no basta con poner not delante («I not like»), necesitamos la palabrita ayudante do. Es como un amigo que viene a ayudar al verbo cuando decimos que no.

7. Negative: doesn't

With he, she, it the helper changes to doesn't (does not): «She doesn't like spiders», «My cat doesn't eat vegetables», «It doesn't snow in Seville».

Very important: the -s goes to doesn't, so the verb loses its -s. We say «He doesn't play», never «He doesn't plays». En castellano: la «s» no puede estar dos veces. Si ya la lleva does, el verbo vuelve a su forma normal.

8. Pronouncing the -s: /s/, /z/, /ɪz/

When we add -s or -es to a verb with he, she or it, it doesn't always sound the same. There are three sounds:

  • /s/, like a snake: after the sounds p, t, k, f.
    stops, eats, likes, walks, laughs.
  • /z/, like a bee (bzzz): after most other sounds, and after vowels.
    plays, reads, lives, runs, goes, sees.
  • /ɪz/, an extra syllable: after the sounds s, z, sh, ch, x and dge.
    watches, washes, kisses, fixes, dances, changes.

The third group is the most important, because the verb has one more syllable: watch (1 syllable) → watch-es (2 syllables). dance (1) → dan-ces (2).

Practise with these tongue twisters:

  • «She watches and washes and fixes the boxes.»
  • «He plays and reads and runs and sees.»
  • «It eats and sleeps and walks and talks.»

Don't worry if it's difficult at first: listening and repeating is the best way to learn.

9. Time words

The present simple often comes with time words that show repetition: every day (todos los días), every week, on Mondays (los lunes), at the weekend (el fin de semana), in summer.

They usually go at the end of the sentence: «I have English on Tuesdays», «We go to the beach in summer». En castellano: fíjate que en inglés los días de la semana se escriben siempre con mayúscula: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday… ¡En español no!

10. Facts about the world

We use the present simple for habits, but also for facts (hechos): things that are always true.

Facts about nature:

  • «The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.»
  • «Water boils at 100 degrees.»
  • «The Earth goes round the Sun.»
  • «Bees make honey.»
  • «Cows eat grass.»
  • «Penguins live in the Antarctic.»

Facts about countries and people:

  • «People in Brazil speak Portuguese.»
  • «It rains a lot in Ireland.»
  • «The river Ebro flows into the Mediterranean Sea.»

Facts about you:

  • «I live in Murcia.» «My mum works in a hospital.» «My brother studies at university.»

And negative facts:

  • «Penguins don't fly.»
  • «A spider doesn't have six legs. It has eight!»
  • «The Moon doesn't give light. It reflects the light of the Sun.»

Facts don't need time words like today or now, because they are true every day: yesterday, today and tomorrow. That's why science books, encyclopedias and documentaries use the present simple all the time. Look for facts in your science book and read them in English!

Game: say a fact. Is it true or false? «Fish breathe with lungs.» → False! Fish breathe with gills.

11. Reading: my family's habits

Read Daniel's text: «My family is very busy. My mum works in a hospital. She starts work at seven. My dad teaches maths. He doesn't drive to work: he goes by bus. My sister Ana studies a lot and she plays the piano. I don't play the piano, but I love football. We all have dinner together at eight. My grandpa lives with us and he watches the news every night.»

Find three verbs with -s, one with -es and one with -ies. Who doesn't drive?

12. Let's practise: true or false?

Play this game in pairs. Write four sentences about your partner, two affirmative and two negative: «Carla likes cats», «Carla doesn't eat fish». Then read them aloud. Your partner says «True!» or «False!» and corrects you: «False! I don't like cats. I like dogs».

Consejo: antes de leer, revisa cada frase. Si el sujeto es él o ella, ¿lleva el verbo la s? En las negativas con doesn't, ¿has quitado la s del verbo? Si lo haces bien, ¡ganas un punto!

13. Writing about a family member

Let's write a short description of someone in our family, using the present simple. Follow this plan:

  1. Introduction: who is it? «This is my aunt Carmen. She is thirty-five years old. She lives in Seville.»
  2. Appearance: «She is tall and she has got long black hair and brown eyes.»
  3. Job and routine: «She is a vet (veterinaria). She works in an animal hospital. She gets up at seven and she starts work at eight.»
  4. Likes and dislikes: «She loves dancing flamenco and she likes cooking. She doesn't like cold weather.»
  5. Why you like this person: «She is very funny and she always tells me stories about animals. I love visiting her!»

Checklist before you finish:

  • Did you add -s to the verbs with he or she? (She lives, she works, she loves.)
  • Did you use doesn't in negatives? (She doesn't like…)
  • Did you use -ing after like, love and hate?
  • Did you start each sentence with a capital letter and finish with a full stop?
  • Did you use and and but to join ideas?

Add a photo or a drawing, and your description is ready!

14. Present simple questions review

Let's review the questions in the present simple. Remember: we use do or does at the beginning.

  • Do + I / you / we / they + verb: «Do you live near the school?»
  • Does + he / she / it + verb (without -s!): «Does she live near the school?» Not «Does she lives…».

Short answers:

  • «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»
  • «Yes, she does.» / «No, she doesn't.»

Wh- questions (with question words) go before do / does:

  • «Where do you live?» → «I live in Toledo.»
  • «What does your dad do?» → «He's a taxi driver.» (This question asks about the job!)
  • «When do you play tennis?» → «On Fridays.»
  • «What time does the film start?» → «At six o'clock.»
  • «How do you go to school?» → «On foot.» / «By bus.»

A trick: in the question, the -s goes to does, not to the verb. It can't be in two places at the same time!

Now interview a friend: ask five questions with do and five with does about your friend's family.

Present simple

Ejercicios

  1. Write the -s form: read, swim, cook.

  2. Write the -es form: wash, go, catch.

  3. Write the third person: study, cry, play.

  4. Complete: «My brother ___ (have) a bike.»

  5. Complete with don't or doesn't: «We ___ like rain.»

  6. Complete with don't or doesn't: «The baby ___ walk.»

  7. Make it negative: «Lola speaks French.»

  8. Correct: «He don't watch TV.»

  9. Translate: «Mi gato duerme en el sofá.»

  10. Write two true sentences about a friend (one negative).

  11. Complete: I ___ (like) reading comics.

  12. Complete: He ___ (hate) getting up early.

  13. True or false: Bees make honey.

  14. Write the -ing form of swim and dance.

  15. Complete: ___ your sister like cats?

  16. Which sound has the -s in «washes»?

  17. Correct: She don't like football.

  18. Write two facts about animals.

  19. Answer: Does Zoe like football?

  20. Write a question with Where for «I live in Toledo».

  21. Write a description of a family member (5 sentences).

  22. Write three true and three false facts for a quiz.

  23. Make a chart: what your classmates love and hate.

  24. Interview a friend with five do/does questions.

Practica

  1. «She ___ comics.»

    1. A) read
    2. B) reades
    3. C) reads

  2. «They ___ in Valencia.»

    1. A) live
    2. B) lives
    3. C) livs

  3. The -s form of «watch» is…

    1. A) watchs
    2. B) watches
    3. C) watchies

  4. The -s form of «study» is…

    1. A) studys
    2. B) studies
    3. C) studyes

  5. «He ___ a sister.»

    1. A) haves
    2. B) have
    3. C) has

  6. «I ___ like spiders.»

    1. A) don't
    2. B) doesn't
    3. C) not

  7. «My dog ___ eat apples.»

    1. A) don't
    2. B) isn't
    3. C) doesn't

  8. Which is correct?

    1. A) He doesn't plays.
    2. B) He doesn't play.
    3. C) He don't play.

  9. We use the present simple for…

    1. A) habits
    2. B) what is happening now
    3. C) the past

  10. Which is written correctly?

    1. A) on Monday
    2. B) on monday
    3. C) On monday

  11. I love ___ .

    1. A) swim
    2. B) swimming
    3. C) swims

  12. She ___ like football.

    1. A) don't
    2. B) isn't
    3. C) doesn't

  13. «Watches» has the sound…

    1. A) /s/
    2. B) /ɪz/
    3. C) /z/

  14. Water ___ at 100 degrees.

    1. A) boils
    2. B) boil
    3. C) boiling

  15. ___ your dad work in a shop?

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Is
    3. C) Does

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el presente simple; Por qué el verbo lleva -s con he, she, it; Las reglas de -s, -es, -ies y el verbo has; Cómo se forma la negativa con don't y doesn't.

Soluciones

  1. C) she + s.
  2. A) they sin s.
  3. B) -ch + es.
  4. B) consonante + y → ies.
  5. C) have → has.
  6. A) I + don't.
  7. C) dog = it.
  8. B) Sin s tras doesn't.
  9. A) Costumbres.
  10. A) Días con mayúscula.
  11. B) Like / love + ing.
  12. C) Negative.
  13. B) Pronunciation.
  14. A) Facts.
  15. C) Questions.
